purpose: Resolve the first-line Shokaku/Zuikaku/Hiryu dawn strike after the overnight/pre-dawn GO gate opens, using the surviving post-GALVANIC carrier cadre, Kinsei mix, US CIC/F6F/AA superiority and explicit mission-split geometry.

japanese_force.reserve_rule: Remainder is CAP, recovery reserve, maintenance/spares and local search; 219 is not a 219-plane strike.

target_ground_truth.state: Early-morning land-strike launch/recovery cycle with heavy CAP/ASW because Japanese carriers remain unlocated.

timeline.event: Japanese strike launches and forms under radio discipline; carrier force turns westward after launch to preserve egress.
US radar/CIC detects the incoming raid roughly 85-105 nmi out and vectors staged F6F CAP. Neighboring-group fighters can only reinforce at the edge of the engagement because groups remain separated.

F6F interception breaks formations and destroys many attack aircraft, but Kinsei/late-Zuisei escorts preserve several release groups. Surviving D4Y/B6N attack through very heavy battleship/cruiser/destroyer AA.

centered_damage.Cabot_CVL28: One aerial torpedo hit centered, aft/machinery-shaft flooding and local fires. Survives but loses useful fast-carrier operations for the current Marshall battle and requires rearward repair assessment.
centered_damage.Intrepid_CV11: One bomb hit centered near flight-deck/elevator-side working area plus splinter damage; flight operations interrupted for several hours but propulsion retained and limited deck operations recover later in the day.
centered_damage.other_major_US_ships: Near-miss/splinter damage only centered; no fast battleship mission kill.

air_losses.US_note: Includes F6F combat losses plus several aircraft destroyed/damaged aboard the hit carriers; not all are air-to-air kills.

assessment: Japan achieves a real operational hit on one CVL and temporary disruption of one fleet carrier, but pays a severe attack-aircraft/cadre cost. The target group remains afloat and its battleship/AA screen remains intact.
anti_overreach: Kinsei narrows local fighter losses but does not defeat US CIC/F6F system
No second Japanese strike is launched before recovery and counterstrike risk are resolved
